links.outcome: AI CAD vs radiologists diagnostic yield and PPV on same CXRs
links.effect: CAD DYD 229/273 (83.9%) vs radiologists 70/273 (25.6%); CAD PPV 1.7% vs radiologists 10.3%; CAD captured all 70 radiologist-detected cases.
links.quote: Among the 273 patients with confirmed PTB, CAD achieved DYD of 83.9% (229/273), which was substantially higher than that of radiologists (70/273, 25.6%).

links.outcome: CAD performance by health care facility tier (county vs township)
links.effect: CAD performed worse in county-level hospitals (DYD 62.5%, PPV 0.6%) than township facilities (DYD 86.7%, PPV 2%), P<.001.
links.quote: However, CAD showed significant variation in performance with respect to health care facility tier, performing poorer in the county-level group than in the township-level group ( P <.001; Table S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1 ).

links.outcome: CAD false positives and positive rate in low-prevalence symptomatic population
links.effect: CAD flagged 13,515 (14.5%) as positive with PPV 1.7% at 0.3% prevalence, versus radiologist positive rate 0.7%.
links.quote: However, excessive reliance on CAD-based diagnoses may potentially contribute to a higher volume of unnecessary follow-up procedures, leading to an inefficient allocation of medical resources.

links.outcome: CAD performance across subgroups (age, sex, region, patient category)
links.effect: CAD outperformed radiologists in all subgroups; age ≥80 less likely to have high PPV (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.10-0.44); no sex or inpatient/outpatient differences.
links.quote: Multivariate logistic regression also demonstrated that advanced age (≥80 y) groups were less likely to achieve high PPV (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.10‐0.44; P <.001).

links.outcome: Radiologist review of CAD-positive images only (triage) workload and cases missed
links.effect: Selective review of CAD-positive images reduced radiologist workload by 85.5% (13,515 of 93,319 CXRs) without missing any radiologist-identified PTB cases.
links.quote: Strategy 5 enabled a radiologist workload reduction of 85.5% (1‐13,515/93,319) while maintaining a minimum system DYD of 25.6% (ie, finding all cases the radiologists originally found) and a potential DYD of 83.9% (if radiologists trusted the AI on all 229 positive cases; Table 2 ).

links.outcome: AI score quartiles for prioritizing radiologist review of high-risk patients
links.effect: Scores >0.75 (34.2% of CAD-positive) contained 189/229 (82.5%) of confirmed PTB cases; P for trend <.001.
links.quote: Most confirmed patients (189/229, 82.5%) had CAD scores exceeding the 75% quantiles (Q75) threshold, which accounted for 34.2% (4618/13,515) of all CAD-positive patients ( Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Local real-world performance of AI on retrospective local data versus reference standard
links.effect: On local historical CXRs versus bacteriological confirmation, CAD DYD was 83.9% versus 78.9% in prior clinical validation, noting a difference in primary care performance.
links.quote: Compared with the sensitivity shown in clinical validation (eg, 78.9% in a study by Yang et al [ 12 ]), there is still a certain difference in performance in primary health care.
